import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 197

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/197](https://www.erdosproblems.com/197)
-/

open Set

namespace Erdos197

/--
Can $\mathbb{N}$ be partitioned into two sets, each of which can be permuted to avoid monotone
3-term arithmetic progressions?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_197 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ A B : Set ℕ, IsCompl A B ∧
      (∃ f : ℕ ≃ A, ¬HasMonotoneAP (Subtype.val ∘ f) 3) ∧
      (∃ g : ℕ ≃ B, ¬HasMonotoneAP (Subtype.val ∘ g) 3) := by
  sorry

end Erdos197

reformulations.difference: The equivalences ℕ ≃ A and ℕ ≃ B require both partition classes to be infinite, whereas the source simply asks for two sets that can be permuted.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Finite classes cannot participate in a successful partition. If one class were finite, the other would be cofinite. Every enumeration of a cofinite subset contains an increasing 3-term AP: choose C such that every integer at least C belongs to the subset; let a be the first term and b the first term exceeding max(a,C). Then c = 2b − a > b belongs to the subset and must occur after b, giving the subsequence a,b,c. Two finite classes cannot cover ℕ either. Thus allowing finite permutations adds no possible witnesses. The full equivalence with a formulation allowing either Fin n-indexed or ℕ-indexed permutations was proved as Review197.partition_finite_or_infinite_iff in /workspace/review/ap_checks.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean's ℕ includes zero, while Adenwalla's corresponding partition question is stated for the positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Translation n ↦ n + 1 bijectively transports partitions of ℕ to partitions of the positive integers and transports each enumeration without changing its index order. It preserves and reflects arithmetic progressions; the inverse subtracts one only from positive values. The full partition-existence equivalence was proved as Review197.nat_iff_positive in /workspace/review/ap_checks.lean.

review.notes: Checked the file's sole declaration. IsCompl gives exactly disjointness and exhaustive union. Lean checks establish that HasMonotoneAP f 3 is equivalent to the existence of indices i < j < k with f i + f k = 2*f j; injectivity of the enumerations excludes zero-step progressions. Both progression orientations are included, and indices need not be consecutive. Finite-list tests passed.
